items.period: Shang dynasty oracle-bone script; specimen reference 前2.32.4 / 合37459 per the previously inspected Commons and Academia Sinica records
items.caption: This oracle-script form of 八 has two long, slightly curved strokes that open downward. Oracle-bone inscriptions already use 八 as a numeral; the traditional separation interpretation remains disputed.
items.alt: Two long curved strokes opening downward, with the right stroke taller than the left.
items.selection_reason: The clear, sourced oracle-script example illustrates the early graph while its shape alone does not settle the proposed origin.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as stated on the Commons file page for the redraw and cited source picture.

items.period: Warring States bronze-script style; source cited as 丙辰方壺 西清19·3
items.caption: This Warring States bronze-script form also has two strokes opening downward, with the left stroke curving more strongly outward. It offers a graphic comparison but does not resolve the graph’s origin.
items.alt: Two curved strokes opening downward and outward; the left stroke extends lower than the right.
items.selection_reason: This legible, separately sourced bronze-script example adds a useful comparison without implying a sequence of change.
items.rights: Public domain; the Commons file page states the representation is released for unrestricted reuse.

limitations.text: Both images are modern vector redraws, not photographs of inscribed artifacts. Their shapes do not establish what 八 originally represented or whether a proposed separation sense preceded its attested numeral use.
